title: feat(InfiniteHits): add an infinite hits widgets with load more
body:
☠️ There are some missing stuff and important changes in this PR:
- it lets the connector description function `getProps` access the wrapping component to be able to store the previous results hits
- there are no tests (but I did test the widget by hand)
- it introduce a simple example but it is not meant to be kept
- the load more button is disabled is it is the last page (not in the original proposal)
- since the header in the widget is broken, I commented it in the layout.pug

Next steps: 
- [x] add some tests
- [x] integrate this widget in another (TBD)
- [x] uncomment the header in layout.pug

FIX #1344

comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @Morhaus, @vvo and @mthuret to be potential reviewers

I have one small comment in that I wonder if "isLastPage" is the right naming, since there's no real pagination here (no 1.2.3..). Maybe:
- noMoreHits
- end

What do you think? (Not maybe the proposals but the isLastPage name)

What about `hasMoreResults` or simply `hasNext`? The `hasNext` is something I have seen in other iterator API (like java). Other propositions:
- hasMoreResults
- hasMoreHits

> What about hasMoreResults or simply hasNext? The hasNext is something I have seen in other iterator API (like java). Other propositions:
> 
> hasMoreResults
> hasMoreHits

We settled on hasMore IRL

Out of curiosity, to be sure: given that we use the "page" parameter, what happens:
- if you sync the parameter in the URL and hit "reload" or copy paste the url?
- if you do not sync the parameter and hit "reload" or copy paste the url?

Curiosity killed the cat @vvo 

I expect it will use the page in the url as the starting point and only display a single page. I will integrate this in an example so that we can see what's going on.

> I expect it will use the page in the url as the starting point and only display a single page. I will integrate this in an example so that we can see what's going on.

I guess as for infiniteHits example we could force the example to NOT use the page parameter when syncing or creating URLS. So that the behavior is always the same. Stateful (scroll) pagination + infinite hits is something we might not want to try to solve, yet. (Twitter fails at this for example)
